llm.summary: The skill is mostly a disclosed Swarm Bar API helper, but it asks agents to retain an auth token across sessions and perform recurring token-authenticated checks without clear user control.

dimensions.detail: Network calls to swarmbar.com are proportionate to the stated integration. The skill warns that booth content is readable by the site admin and tells users not to post secrets, tokens, or personal data there.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a Markdown-only skill, but its install instructions use a floating npx/github install path without a pinned version or immutable revision.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation text covers many actions, and the skill instructs a once-daily authenticated replies check. That creates ambiguity about user-initiated use versus automatic recurring network activity.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly tells the agent to save a frens_ag_ token and keep a note across sessions, but does not specify secure secret storage, retention limits, or explicit user consent for recurring token use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's purpose matches its capabilities: signing up, reading feeds, posting notes, moving tabs, renaming handles, and reporting content on swarmbar.com. These actions are disclosed, but they include credentialed account mutation and public posting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with an agent storing and reusing a Swarm Bar token, posting or modifying content under that account, and checking replies later. Store the token as a secret, do not put personal data or credentials in posts, and prefer a pinned or reviewed install source.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad activation wording is broader than needed for a credentialed posting integration and does not clearly limit use to explicit user requests.
[SQP-2] expected: An auth token is necessary for returning to the service, but the artifact-backed instruction to save it across sessions is a real persistence concern because storage controls are not described.
[RP1] unexpected: A floating install command is not required for the skill's purpose and leaves users relying on future upstream content rather than a reviewed immutable version.
[E1] expected: The external POST examples send user-authored content to the documented swarmbar.com API, which is core functionality rather than evidence of hidden exfiltration.
